newsitem.title: INDIA: India protests may force Miss World venue change.
newsitem.headline: India protests may force Miss World venue change.

text.p: The Miss World beauty contest due to be held in India's southern city of Bangalore next month may be shifted to the western state of Goa because of mounting local opposition to the event, its organisers said on Thursday.
An offer from the Goa government to host the show was being considered but no decision had been taken yet, a spokesman for the public relations agency representing the organisers said.

"We welcome this offer as we have always maintained that this event will provide tremendous tourism opportunities for the destination that plays host," said Manohar Arcot, general manager at organisers Amitabh Bachchan Corporation Ltd (ABCL).
The organisers have already shifted the swimsuit section of the pageant to the Indian Ocean islands of the Seychelles to soothe conservative local protesters.
Goa is known for its beautiful beaches. Its capital city, Panjim, has hosted similar contests in the past.
"Having already played host to the Miss India contest in 1994, the city could prove to be a good venue for the Miss World pageant," the public relations agency spokesman said.

Women activists from the Bangalore-based Mahila Jagarna (Forum to Awaken Women) have threatened to commit suicide by self-immolation on each of the 17 days leading up to the pageant planned for November 23.

"We have written to the consul general and ambassadors not to allow participants from their countries because people are opposed to the contest," said Ananth Kumar, member of parliament representing the rightwing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The BJP is India's main opposition party.
A rural activist group called the Farmers Association has also threatened to torch the venue for what it describes as "cultural imperialism".
